text:
Alex: Hey team — seeing a new tail-latency regression on the dedicated pools after the batching tweak. 95p latency up ~2.3x for small requests. I captured an nsys trace: https://artifacts/redwood/nsys/2143654321-capture.qdlt :thinking_face:
Maria: Thanks Alex. Any quick observations from the timeline?
Alex: Quick skim: lots of tiny H2D memcpy bursts interleaved with kernels. memcpy slices look like 200-500us each and they appear on a stream that should be for copies, but they serialize kernels on the compute stream somehow. CPU slices show the host thread stalled/scheduled out right before submit for several ms.
Jun: Could be pageable->pinned fallback. If buffers are pageable cudaMemcpyAsync will sync with default stream on some drivers and cause implicit sync. Also if host thread gets preempted, submission jitter accumulates.
Priya: Flag: our batching heuristic started emitting more microbatches to reduce queueing. That increases frequency of H2D submissions. We probably didn't ensure pinned allocation for those transient buffers.
Maria: Can you paste the nsys command you used? I'll take a peek.
Alex: Sure — ran:
```
nsys profile -o microbatch-debug --capture-range=cpu:profile -t cuda,cudnn,osrt --trace-fork=false ./run_benchmark --workload=canary-small
```
Also exported a perfetto timeline snippet.
Jun: In the timeline I see these patterns: (1) tiny h2d memcpy on stream 3, (2) a kernel on stream 0 that only starts after memcpy finishes, (3) the host submit thread shows a 1.2-3ms scheduler gap between recording the NVTX push and enqueue. That gap lines up with the extra latency.
Priya: So two orthogonal issues: a) pageable copies causing implicit sync/serialization, b) OS-level scheduling causing submit jitter. Fix path: coalesce small copies + ensure pinned pool + set stream priority or use a dedicated high-prio compute stream.
Maria: Agreed. Also consider grouping microbatches into a single large H2D per physical GPU tick — our batcher can emit a coalesced copy for N tiny batches. That should amortize DMA startup overhead and reduce number of host submissions.
Alex: Quick test I ran: forced pinned allocations for the microbatch buffers (mallocHost) — 95p latency dropped from 182ms -> 78ms in the canary. CPU submit gaps shrank a bit too.
Jun: Nice. We should still address host scheduling. Maybe use real-time niceness for the submit thread or pin it to a bthread/rt policy on the Dedicated VMs. BUT be careful with elevated priority in multi-tenant hosts.
Priya: Another mitigation: batcher heuristic change — if microbatch size < 512 tokens, coalesce copies for up to 4 microbatches OR wait up to 300us to allow additional requests to join. That should hit a sweet spot.
Maria: For telemetry, add an nvtx range around the H2D stage with metadata: batch_id, subbatch_count, pinned_flag, buffer_size. That will let us filter traces by whether pinned was used.
Alex: Created a small patch and test harness. Command to reproduce (non-blocking memory behaviour):
```
# run with env to toggle pinned pool
REDWOOD_PINNED_POOL=0 ./run_benchmark --micro 1 --repeat 1000 > /tmp/micro.log
REDWOOD_PINNED_POOL=1 ./run_benchmark --micro 1 --repeat 1000 > /tmp/micro_pinned.log
```
Comparing logs + nsys captures shows the pinned run has far fewer memcpy spikes.
Jun: Also capture `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` maybe for a succinct kernel+memcopy list. nsys timeline is best for scheduling gaps though.
Priya: Action items: (1) Alex to land a non-prod pin-pool toggle and run overnight A/B (2) Maria to prototype coalescing heuristic + a 300us hold window (3) Jun to draft OS-level guidance for submit thread affinity and an experiment to try SCHED_BATCH vs SCHED_FIFO perf (4) Perf-bot to add a regression alert that triggers if 95p increases by >1.5x on dedicated pools.
perf-bot: Created perf-alert ticket INF-9874 and scheduled a nightly compare job: baseline=2143600000, job=canary/microbatch.
Maria: One more note — kernel selection may still hurt if the compute kernels expect large contiguous KV cache regions. If we coalesce copies but change ordering, check the kvcache prefetch offsets. Add a small eval comparing token-level quality and hit-rate.
Alex: Good catch. I'll add kvcache hit-rate logging in the harness.
Priya: TL;DR: root cause likely composite (pageable copy + host scheduling + microbatching churn). Quick wins: enable pinned pool and coalesce. Longer term: batcher heuristics + submit-thread affinity + stream priority mapping.
Alex: Thanks all — I'll post updated nsys captures in ~24h. :thumbsup:
